solved.topic: Fundamental frequency of a stretched string
solved.q: A string of length 0.5 m and linear density (mass per unit length) 0.01 kg/m is stretched with a tension of 100 N. Find the fundamental frequency of vibration.
steps: Given: L = 0.5 m, m = 0.01 kg/m, T = 100 N.

solved.q: The fundamental frequency of a stretched string is 120 Hz. Find the frequency of its third harmonic.
steps: Formula: harmonics of a string are n, 2n, 3n, ... (all integer multiples).

solved.q: An open organ pipe of length 0.66 m resonates in its fundamental mode. If the speed of sound in air is 330 m/s, find the fundamental frequency.
steps: In an open pipe, fundamental: L = lambda/2, so lambda = 2L.

solved.q: A closed organ pipe has a fundamental frequency of 170 Hz. Taking the speed of sound in air as 340 m/s, find the length of the pipe.
steps: In a closed pipe, fundamental: L = lambda/4, so lambda = 4L.
Formula: n = v/lambda = v/(4L), so L = v/(4n).

solved.q: Two tuning forks of frequencies 256 Hz and 254 Hz are sounded together. Find the beat frequency and the time interval between two successive beats.
steps: Time interval between successive beats = 1/(beat frequency) = 1/2.
Beat frequency = 2 Hz; time interval = 0.5 s.
solved.ans: Beat frequency = 2 Hz, time interval = 0.5 s

solved.topic: Effect of tension on frequency of a string
solved.q: A stretched string vibrates with a fundamental frequency of 100 Hz under a tension T. Find the new fundamental frequency if the tension is doubled, keeping length and mass per unit length constant.
steps: Given: n1 = 100 Hz, T2 = 2 x T1, L and m constant.
Formula: n is proportional to sqrt(T), since n = (1/2L)sqrt(T/m).
n2 = 100 x sqrt(2) = 100 x 1.414 (using sqrt(2) = 1.414 from tables).

solved.q: In a resonance tube experiment, the first and second resonance lengths of an air column are found to be 0.17 m and 0.52 m respectively for a tuning fork. Find the wavelength of sound and the end correction of the tube.
steps: Formula: for successive resonances, l2 - l1 = lambda/2, so lambda = 2(l2 - l1).
lambda = 0.70 m, end correction e = 0.005 m.
solved.ans: lambda = 0.70 m, end correction = 0.005 m (0.5 cm)

solved.q: The fundamental frequency of a closed organ pipe is 100 Hz. State and calculate the frequencies of the next two harmonics present in this pipe.
steps: Given: fundamental frequency n = 100 Hz for a closed pipe.
Rule: a closed pipe (closed at one end) supports only odd harmonics: n, 3n, 5n, ...
Next harmonic after fundamental is the 3rd harmonic: 3 x 100 = 300.
Harmonic after that is the 5th harmonic: 5 x 100 = 500.
Next two harmonics present = 300 Hz and 500 Hz (the 2nd and 4th harmonics are absent).

practice.topic: Fundamental frequency and length of string
practice.q: A string vibrating with a fundamental frequency of 100 Hz has its length halved while the tension is kept unchanged. Find the new fundamental frequency.
practice.hint: n = (1/2L)sqrt(T/m); n is inversely proportional to L, so halving L doubles n.

practice.q: An open pipe of length 0.5 m resonates with air. Taking the speed of sound as 340 m/s, find the frequency of the second harmonic of this pipe.
practice.hint: For an open pipe, n_p = p*v/(2L); second harmonic means p = 2.

practice.q: A closed pipe has length 0.25 m. Taking the speed of sound in air as 340 m/s, find its fundamental frequency.
practice.hint: For a closed pipe, fundamental n = v/(4L).

practice.q: Two sound waves of frequencies 300 Hz and 295 Hz are produced simultaneously. Find the beat frequency and the number of beats heard in 10 seconds.
practice.hint: Beat frequency = |n1 - n2|; beats in time t = (beat frequency) x t.
practice.ans: Beat frequency = 5 Hz, beats in 10 s = 50

practice.topic: Effect of tension on string frequency
practice.q: A stretched string has a fundamental frequency of 50 Hz under tension T. Find the new fundamental frequency if the tension is made 4 times the original value, with length and mass per unit length unchanged.
practice.hint: n is proportional to sqrt(T); find n2/n1 = sqrt(T2/T1).

practice.q: A stationary wave is formed with wavelength 0.8 m. Find the distance between two consecutive nodes and between a node and the next antinode.
practice.hint: Distance between consecutive nodes = lambda/2; distance between a node and adjacent antinode = lambda/4.
